document.title: Wireless No-Touch Forehead Thermometer Use Specification and Usability Engineering Summary

products.name: Wireless No-Touch Forehead Thermometer (Infrared Forehead Thermometer)

semantic_fragments.content: The Wireless No-Touch Forehead Thermometer is intended for the intermittent measurement of body temperature from the forehead on people of all ages. It can be used by consumers in the household environment and by healthcare providers.

Intended patient population and operator: The Infrared Forehead Thermometer is suitable for people of all ages, including lay persons and professionals. Intended part of the body: Aim the thermometer probe at the center of the forehead and keep the probe 1.18 in (3cm) away from the forehead (the optimal distance is about the width of an adult's index finger).

Intended USER PROFILE: 1. Experience: minimum: no special experience needed. 2. Age: people of all ages. 3. Education: several years of intensive reading experience (school). 4. Knowledge: minimum: read and understand 'westernized Arabic' numerals in Arial font, can read temperature values and related prompts, understands hygiene. 5. Language understanding: languages as specified in the instruction. 6. Health: The patient can be an intended operator. All functions of the unit can be used safely by patient. 7. User state: User is OPERATOR: alert, mentally competent.

USE ENVIRONMENT: Home use, avoid strong magnetism interference. Environmental temperature for using: 50℉-104℉(10℃-40℃). Environmental humidity for using: 15-95%RH, non-condensing. Environmental temperature for storage: -4℉~131℉（-20℃~55℃）. Environmental humidity for storage: 15-95%RH, non-condensing. Environmental pressure: 70kPa~106kPa. Frequency of use: not specified. Mobility: handheld.
This product is a high-tech infra-red (IR) thermometer designed to take human body temperature by measuring the energy of IR emitted from the forehead.

User interface characteristics related to safety and potential use errors: a) Switching on/off: easy tactile identification of button location. b) Press button and reading display: button easier to identify and press; display clearly visible under conditions of visibility. c) Changing battery: clear indication of proper polarity and battery type; inserting incorrect battery does not damage device; easy battery interchange for elderly with reduced fine motor control. d) Cleaning: no entrapping contours or crevices; clean with soft, slightly moistened cloth, mild soapy water for extreme soiling. e) Storing: no special conditions required. f) Instructions for use: address water/humidity, temperature, battery type and replacement.
User interface characteristics related to safety: When there is an error, the thermometer will produce a visual alarm. There is no rough surface, sharp angle or sharp edge.

Potential use errors and safety risks: 1. Cannot install battery or install in wrong polarity → device does not work. 2. Battery depleted → device does not work. 3. Battery capacity too low → device cannot measure correctly. 4. Measurement distance too long → device cannot measure correctly. 5. Target temperature beyond range 89.6℉-109.2℉(32℃-42.9℃) → device cannot measure correctly. 6. Environment temperature exceeds 50℉-104℉(10℃-40℃) or is unstable → device cannot measure correctly. 7. Cannot turn on device → device will not work. 8. Cannot clean probe → probe life reduced, detection results may be inaccurate. 9. Water enters device during cleaning → device may fail to work. 10. Battery not removed when not used for a long time → battery life decreased. 11. Measuring body parts incorrectly → measurement result inaccurate.

Summary of known use problems - Identifying known or foreseeable hazards: The process follows ISO 14971 RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS and USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS to identify USE ERRORS as potential contributors to HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS. The primary objective is to recognize scenarios where device use could lead to harm by analyzing potential USE ERRORS and their consequences. FDA MAUDE database was searched for adverse events related to Infrared Forehead Thermometer; a few adverse events were found, mostly involving measurement errors. In most cases, no complications resulted and patients were doing well.
